story: Three riders escaped early in the race, before three more competitors bridged across with around 40 kilometres remaining. The breakaway was caught on the Muur van Geraardsbergen, where the race exploded and Segaert and Berckmoes opened a gap. Pithie attempted to close it but was unable to make contact. The leading duo narrowly stayed ahead until Berckmoes attacked on the final hill. He rode alone to the victory and the leader’s jersey, while Philipsen crossed the line a few seconds later to take second place.
